_comment: The structured parameter-naming convention. Shared by param_naming.py (add-ins,
servers) and param_naming.js (the companion windows) — this file is the single
source of truth for both, exactly as variables.json is for the situational engine.
EDITED IN Control Room ▸ Fusion ▸ Parameter Names (remap/server.py's
/param_naming/set); a hand edit here is the same write and is picked up the next
time a window opens a session.
A parameter name has three segments: FEATURE (one or more comma-separated levels —
the part, and the part of the part), TYPE (what kind of measurement), and
ANCHOR/AXIS (which bound it is measured from, or just the axis). Fusion itself only
accepts letters/digits/underscore, so the delimited form the user picks
('BootCeiling,Front-Inset-Back') is joined with '_' to make the real name
('BootCeiling_Front_Inset_Back'). The join is LOSSLESS: parse() recovers the exact
levels/type/anchor a compose() produced, by walking the underscore-split words
backwards — the trailing anchor/axis words (see multi, below), then exactly one
type word, everything left is feature levels.
This is a SEPARATE, newer convention from variables.json's situational-tag engine.
The two are not merged: existing parameters that don't fit this shape (built under
the old convention) simply fail to parse() here and are left alone — a migration
tool handles those later.
_types_comment: A TYPE is one kind of measurement. Its fields:
word     the type word itself, and the name's middle segment. Must not collide
with an anchor word or an axis letter — parsing depends on the two
vocabularies being disjoint.
units    which dimension units this type can measure ('' is unitless). The type
step filters on the dimension's own unit; an unknown unit offers all.
anchor   'required' | 'none'. 'required' asks for a bound word (Back, Left…)
from `anchors` below, which carries an axis AND an end.
axis     'required' | 'optional' | 'none'. 'optional' shows the step but
Enter/Space skips it — Enter also takes it on a step that isn't done
yet; the title line says so in red when there was nothing to take. A
type asks for ONE of anchor or axis, never both: an anchor already
says which axis it is on.
multi    more than one anchor/axis may be chosen — 'X and Y both work'. The name
carries every one of them ('Drawer_Width_Span_X_Y'), and the parameter
is suggested on any of them.
suggest  WHEN this type is offered, and when a parameter named with it is
offered back — see the block below.
note     what the type means, in a sentence. Shown on its Control Room row.
SUGGEST. Two conditions, both judged against the situation the dialog is in (the
dimension's axis, which end of it, and what it is measured FROM):
datum  'any'    — offer it whatever the dimension is measured from.
'origin' — only when the dimension starts at the origin. Offset is the
case: a value measured from nothing in particular only means
something when one of the two points IS the origin.
'bounds' — only when it does NOT. Inset measures in from the model
bounds, so a dimension off the origin is the one it is for.
axis   'same'   — only when the dimension is within 45° of the parameter's own
axis (45° itself counts — a 45° dimension matches BOTH of its
neighbouring axes, and so is offered from either pool), and,
for an anchored type, the matching axis is at the same end. A
parameter that carries NO axis (Span/Thickness left on the
optional axis step) is general and always fits.
'any'    — offer it on every axis regardless — never used by a type that
takes a real axis; kept for one that has none at all to give
(Radius, Multiplier, Angle).
A situation that says nothing never disqualifies anything: a dimension with no
known datum passes every datum rule, exactly as one with no known axis passes
every axis rule. Only a stated disagreement filters.

_comment: How Span's own axis reads back to the user — 'Width - Span' would say nothing
an Inset-anchored name doesn't already say better, so a Span parameter's TYPE
segment becomes these words instead, in displayLeaf/parseLeaf. Span_X -> 'Width';
Span_X_Y -> 'Width, Depth'; a Span with no axis is still spelled 'Span'.

types.note: End to end (midpoint to end on a symmetric axis). The axis is optional — a span with none is offered everywhere; one with an axis reads back as Width/Depth/Height.
From the model bounds inward. Needs a real anchor, not just an axis.
From no bounds at all — one of the two points is the origin.
Between any two points. The axis is optional — set one and it only offers back on that axis; left off, it fits any direction.
A fillet, a hole, a rounded corner.
Between one repeat and the next.
How many, along an axis or in general.
A ratio applied to another value.
Orientation (+90°, flipped, …) is per-use arithmetic on the chip, not here.
